biography: João Carlos Palhares, a name synonymous with flamboyant Brazilian racing, hails from the vibrant streets of São Paulo. His journey began not on a racetrack, but on the chaotic roads of his city, delivering pizzas at breakneck speeds on a battered moped. It was during these high-stakes deliveries, dodging buses and outsmarting traffic, that his innate racing instincts were honed. A chance encounter with a local karting team owner, impressed by João's daring maneuvers, led to his first competitive drive. Early success in karting propelled him through the ranks, eventually landing him a seat in a regional Formula series. While his raw speed was undeniable, his aggressive style often led to costly mistakes. However, with age and experience, João has tempered his approach, finding a balance between risk and reward. Now at 36, he finds himself in his peak, driving for his self-owned 'Joao Palhares' team, determined to prove that passion and talent can overcome even the most established giants of motorsport.
drivingStyle: João's driving style is a visceral blend of aggression and finesse. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers, often diving into corners where others fear to tread. While his tire management was initially a weakness, he's worked diligently to improve, now capable of extracting maximum performance from his rubber without sacrificing longevity. Under pressure, João thrives, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest. His 'go-for-broke' attitude makes him a thrilling, if sometimes unpredictable, competitor.

careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2021 due to a mechanical failure, robbing him of a likely victory.
